params.body:
The handler keeps a list of exceptions it does not send an error mail about. That list is shorter
than it reads, in the same way as the fifty-six catch blocks removed this morning: a name that does
not resolve, and PHP answering `false` to `instanceof` without a word.

```php
if ($e instanceof ValidateException) {   // no such class; the import says ValidationException
    return false;
}
```

So **every form a dealer filled in wrongly sent an error report by mail** — precisely what that line
was written to prevent. A few lines up, `$exception instanceof Illuminate\Auth\AuthenticationException`
resolves to `App\Exceptions\Illuminate\Auth\AuthenticationException` inside this namespace, so an
unauthenticated request kept being reported as a fault of ours as well.

Both now name the class they meant. `ErrorMailTest` pins which exceptions are worth a mail and which
are a dealer mistyping a chassis number, including the way a validation failure really arrives (a
validator that fails, not a hand-made exception). Checked by putting the typo back: two of the four
tests fail.

Two entries leave the PHPStan baseline, which is where these two had been sitting quietly since
yesterday.

**On the wider question this came from** — should we not be handling these exceptions instead of
deleting the handling? The short answer is that a controller is the wrong place. Let it reach the
handler, where the policy lives in one place; catch only where you can do something the handler
cannot, such as giving the dealer a sentence he can act on, and then catch the specific type rather
than `Exception`. Laravel already answers JSON to a request that expects JSON, so most of the
"the modal needs JSON" catches were never needed either.

What is worth doing next, in order: production reports nothing to Nightwatch (every one of the
fifteen issues there comes from staging), and handling what you cannot see is theatre; then decide
between `ErrorMail` and Nightwatch, because two channels for the same event means nobody reads
either; and only then add specific catches where a dealer deserves a sentence instead of an error
page.

params.title: Two checks in the error handler that never matched
